how to center a div in css

how to center content with flexbox
a: Flexbox makes centering trivial. On the parent container, set `display: flex` and `justify-content: center` (horizontal alignment) together with `align-items: center` (vertical alignment). For a single child, this centers it perfectly. The child does not need any centering properties. This approach works regardless of the child's dimensions.

how to center with css grid
a: CSS Grid provides even more concise centering. Set `display: grid` on the parent with `place-items: center` (shorthand for `align-items: center` and `justify-items: center`). Alternatively, set `place-content: center` on the parent or `place-self: center` on the child for more granular control. All methods work responsively.

how to use css clamp for responsive typography
a: Responsive design relies on three pillars: fluid grids (use `%`, `fr`, `vw`/`vh` instead of fixed pixels), flexible images (`max-width: 100%`), and media queries (`@media (max-width: 768px)`). Use the `clamp()` function for fluid typography that scales between min and max values. Mobile-first design starts with the small screen layout then adds complexity via `min-width` media queries. CSS Grid with `auto-fit`/`auto-fill` and `minmax()` creates auto-responsive layouts without media queries.

q: how to structure an html document
html head body meta tags example
a: Semantic HTML elements clearly describe their meaning to both the browser and developer. Key elements: `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<section>`, `<article>`, `<aside>`, `<footer>`, `<figure>`, `<figcaption>`, `<time>`. Use `<div>` and `<span>` only for styling hooks when no semantic element fits. Semantic HTML improves accessibility (screen readers), SEO, and code maintainability. Always include `lang`, `charset`, and `viewport` meta tags.
